#5241. Ripple's RLUSD Overtakes PayPal's PYUSD

Ripple's US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD has set a new record by surpassing PayPal USD (PYUSD) in market capitalization to cement its position as a top stablecoin globally.

Recent data from CoinGecko shows that RLUSD's market cap has grown to around $2.71 billion, enabling it to surpass its competitor, PayPal's stablecoin, with a market cap of around $2.69 billion.

This milestone was achieved less than two years after Ripple's formal introduction of RLUSD in December 2024, underscoring its rapid growth in the crypto market.

A prominent XRP Ledger validator, Vet, also commented on this development to underscore the increasing significance of RLUSD in the stablecoin industry.

"RLUSD is now a Top 5 USD backed stablecoin. On its way to be in Top 3," Vet commented.

Vet noted Ripple's long-standing contribution to building the XRP Ledger. He added that the increasing adoption of RLUSD could potentially lead to faster adoption of the blockchain by traditional financial institutions.

Vet stressed the increasing relevance of RLUSD's rising payment volume and increased use of the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.

He also noted that RLUSD has opened the door to numerous integrations with banks and crypto exchanges.

The XRP Ledger validator further noted that these integrations could motivate financial institutions to not only run infrastructure to support the XRPL but also integrate other tokenized assets on it.

This new record for RLUSD comes on the back of several key institutional partnerships and exchange integrations for RLUSD that Ripple has been announcing recently.

On Oct. 28, Ripple announced a partnership with Coinbase to provide RLUSD for retail and institutional users across Coinbase Exchange, Coinbase Prime and its retail trading app.

As part of the partnership, Coinbase also announced support for RLUSD across different blockchain networks such as the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

On the other hand, Ripple's partnership with banking giant BNY, which is the custodian of reserves for RLUSD, is also deepening.

Besides this, Ripple has also managed to secure support from Standard Chartered, which launched institutional custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger back in October.

#5240. XRP, ETH, DOGE: Tim Draper Predicts Bitcoin to Absorb Altcoins

Billionaire and longtime Bitcoin (BTC) supporter Tim Draper predicts a future where Bitcoin absorbs the innovations of other altcoins.

Draper's statement has major implications for big cryptocurrencies like XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE), which have built their own ecosystems and now compete in the wider cryptocurrency market.

In a recent post on X, Draper compared Bitcoin's rising dominance to Microsoft's path to becoming the dominant software company, as the company absorbed successful innovations from other businesses.

"Microsoft never invented the spreadsheet, word processor, or slide deck. They absorbed them," stated Draper.

The billionaire investor brought up pioneering software like Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect, which eventually saw their dominance give way to Microsoft's Excel and Word.

Draper predicts that this could apply to the cryptocurrency industry, as Bitcoin could become the ultimate absorber of innovations from alternative blockchain networks.

"Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this time," wrote Draper.

Smaller cryptocurrencies are thus essentially incubators for technological innovations that could eventually become part of the bigger Bitcoin ecosystem, according to Draper.

"They show that it works, then the innovation that pulls the strongest gets ported to the Bitcoin platform," he added.

Draper also supported his statement by citing the rising market share of Bitcoin in the overall cryptocurrency market.

The billionaire investor recalled observing how Bitcoin dominance rose from about 40% to 50% and then even further to 61%.

"Bitcoin is that platform," said Draper, claiming that the biggest cryptocurrency could follow a path similar to Microsoft's.

This statement has implications for the future of big altcoins like Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin.

Ethereum is the leading smart contract and dApp platform, while XRP is mainly known for its cross-border payments and the wider XRP Ledger ecosystem. Meanwhile, Dogecoin is one of the most iconic meme coins in the cryptocurrency market.

Still, the growing ecosystem around Bitcoin, which adds more scaling and programmability through solutions such as the Lightning Network and projects like Stacks, shows how Bitcoin is trying to expand beyond its basic use case as a cryptocurrency.

#5238. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

#5236. Gold Bull Peter Schiff Sees Bitcoin Crashing Toward Cycle Lows Near $59,500

American stockbroker Peter Schiff has warned of an imminent Bitcoin crash following the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

Speaking to his followers on X, the well-known economic and capital markets analyst warned of a potential Bitcoin plunge.

His remarks suggested that BTC is set to lose resilience due to recent events that have eroded investor confidence and pushed crypto prices lower.

Based on his market observation, the analyst noted that since the recently concluded 2026 midterm elections, U.S. stock markets have surged around 12% while Bitcoin dropped by 4.6%. Over the same period, gold and silver prices have risen by 5% and 7%, respectively.

According to Peter Schiff, price hikes in equities, gold, and silver indicate that Wall Street and traditional investors are celebrating the election outcome, marked by Democrats winning control of both the House and Senate.

Initially, investors feared a lengthy political battle after the Democratic sweep. However, traditional capital assets rebounded after Trump accepted the outcome, dispelling fears of an election dispute. In short, investors expect a divided Congress to clamp down on government spending and borrowing.

Also, the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note dropped by 4.91% following the Democratic victory. This means lower Treasury yields support stock valuations by reducing borrowing costs and eroding bond returns, making them less attractive relative to equities and precious metals. This explains strong gains in U.S. stocks and rare metals.

Bitcoin weakened after the midterm election, noting that the timing indicates that the vote and the subsequent Binance hack impacted investor sentiment. Today, BTC trades at $73,135, after losing a crucial support at $75,000 and falling from its recent $80,000 peak.

Paraguay’s electricity market is becoming increasingly competitive, and Bitcoin News is starting to highlight a growing problem for miners. The country’s mining industry is expected to generate approx. $350 million in electricity revenue for state utility ANDE this year, making the battle for hydropower particularly significant.

While AI infrastructure developers are securing long-term power agreements, existing cryptocurrency mining operations face a significant contractual deadline in 2027.

The contrast became clearer in October 2026, when Paraguay’s state-owned electricity utility ANDE signed a 15-year electricity supply agreement with Kuntur S.A. for an AI infrastructure project requiring up to 286 megawatts (MW). The Kuntur agreement provides electricity supply over 15 years, with deliveries scheduled to begin at 6 MW on December 1, 2026. Capacity will gradually increase, reaching the full 286 MW by April 2029.

That’s a substantial commitment. More importantly, it highlights how AI data centers are becoming serious competitors for Paraguay’s hydroelectric power.

The arrangement stands in contrast to HIVE Digital Technologies’ existing electricity agreements, which have a much closer expiration date.

HIVE operates approximately 300 MW of infrastructure across two Paraguayan facilities: 200 MW at Yguazú and 100 MW at Valenzuela.

According to its 2026 annual report, the electricity purchase agreements covering both facilities expire on December 31, 2027.

That’s not a minor contractual detail. Continued operations beyond that date depend on renegotiating existing agreements or securing replacement electricity arrangements on commercially acceptable terms.

HIVE’s position illustrates the uncertainty facing large-scale Paraguay Bitcoin mining operations as competition for electricity intensifies.

The situation doesn’t automatically mean Bitcoin miners will lose access to electricity. However, the difference in contract duration raises questions about future power availability and operating costs.

For BTC miners, securing affordable electricity remains essential to maintaining operations. AI infrastructure developers, meanwhile, are demonstrating their willingness to commit to longer-term electricity arrangements.

The next two years could therefore become important for Paraguay’s mining industry. HIVE’s December 2027 deadline is approaching, while Kuntur has already secured a 15-year agreement.

For Bitcoin News, the bigger story isn’t simply the expansion of AI infrastructure. It’s whether established mining operators can secure equally dependable electricity arrangements before their existing contracts expire.

Bitcoin expert Anthony Pompliano today tackled a crucial question that serious Bitcoin investors often ask. The question is: between hardware wallets and ETFs, which one offers the best outcome for securing and getting exposure to Bitcoin?

In an interview released early today, the celebrated crypto analyst answered questions savvy investors want answered about Bitcoin self-custody versus Bitcoin ETFs.

Today, Bitcoin adoption grows at a remarkable rate. As more investors seek to invest in the cryptocurrency, there are two major ways to do so: gaining exposure through Bitcoin hardware wallets (self-custody) or Bitcoin ETFs.

In the podcast, Pompliano admitted that using spot ETFs is more secure than storing Bitcoin in a hardware wallet. According to the crypto expert, spot ETFs offer an accessible approach, providing investors with a simplified, regulated way to buy and invest in Bitcoin through their existing brokerage accounts. As Pompliano stated, ETFs stand out because they emphasize the importance of regulation in providing investor protection and market integrity.

Pompliano further recognized spot ETFs as the safest and the most convenient option for investors holding between $10,000 and $10 million worth of BTC. He said these investment vehicles offer greater liquidity than directly holding BTC on hardware wallets. They provide investors with diversified exposure to stock exchanges and on-chain markets.

However, he said convenience comes with caveats, as ETFs provide indirect exposure to Bitcoin. This means that investors don’t actually own the underlying Bitcoin. Also, ETFs might not provide investors with the same level of control as directly owning BTC in self-custody wallets.

This highlights the advantages of Bitcoin hardware wallets, which allow customers to hold BTC directly, giving them greater control. However, this level of control comes with the responsibility of managing private keys, asset control, and security risks.

Such unfortunate hacking events compel customers to rethink how to secure their BTC while still accessing strong liquidity. The self-custody approach offers direct ownership and control of BTC, though it requires technical know-how and involves greater security risks. On the other hand, ETFs offer a simple, regulated way to gain exposure to the asset, with diversified liquidity. They, however, come with some limitations.

If the situation persists and bulls are unable to stage a quick recovery, the digital currency could see a major price decline the following year as well.

Historically, Bitcoin’s loss-reporting calendar years have been solo occurrences. In most instances when the premier digital currency witnesses a major contraction, like that in the years 2014 (roughly –56% to –58%), 2018 (around –73% to –74%), and 2022 (about –64%), it has followed it up with major gains in 2015, 2019, and 2023, respectively.

#5225. Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Address From 2010 Suddenly Activates With $3.4 Million

A Bitcoin (BTC) address from 2010 has become active after being dormant for over 16 years. The address has transferred around $3.4 million in BTC.

According to blockchain tracking platform Whale Alert, the address held 50 BTC, which was roughly equivalent to $3,442,939 at the time of activation.

The dormant address had been inactive for 16.2 years. Back in BTC's early days, all 50 BTC were worth just $3.

Notably, this wasn’t the only old Bitcoin address that suddenly became active.

According to Whale Alert, another dormant Bitcoin address holding 50 BTC worth roughly $3,442,129 became active after 16.2 years.

The two transfers took place within minutes of each other on Nov. 13. Hence, the total value of the newly activated Bitcoin comes to around $6.89 million.

There’s no confirmation about who owned these wallets. Also, it’s not confirmed if the same individual or entity owns these addresses.

The reason these addresses are significant is that they date back to 2010, which is considered to be the Satoshi era.

In simple terms, the Satoshi era refers to the first few years of Bitcoin, mainly 2009 and 2010. During those years, the pseudonymous founder of Bitcoin, Satoshi Nakamoto, was pretty active in the network's development.

To be precise, Bitcoin came into existence in January 2009. It initially carried a block reward of 50 BTC. This block reward of 50 BTC continued until Bitcoin had its first halving in November 2012.

This is why these newly activated addresses’ holdings of 50 BTC match the rewards miners could receive during the early days of Bitcoin.

These old addresses always raise a lot of interest as Bitcoin had relatively few miners and users during those times.

However, this does not mean that these wallets are owned by the mysterious founder of Bitcoin.

This recent activation comes after a series of interesting activations in the crypto world. These are long-dormant crypto addresses that have become active over the past month.

On Oct. 22, a Bitcoin address with 170 BTC worth roughly $14.38 million became active after being dormant for 13 years, as reported by Whale Alert.

Prior to this, on Oct. 20, a dormant address with 500 BTC worth around $41.54 million became active after 10.7 years. In 2016, these holdings were worth just $194,955.

Later, crypto analytics platform Arkham linked the 500 BTC transaction to addresses belonging to convicted Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins. Previously, his crypto holdings were deemed inaccessible.

On Oct. 17, Whale Alert tracked activity involving old Bitcoin addresses holding 248 BTC and 167 BTC worth roughly $20.24 million and $13.65 million, respectively.

#5218. Crypto Founder Drops Bombshell on XRP’s Ripple Dependency, Challenges Holders to Act as Ambitious $10 Forecast Gains Steam

Flare co-founder Hugo Philion has pushed back against renewed XRP criticism, arguing that the cryptocurrency’s value and long-term narrative should not depend solely on Ripple’s decisions.

This development comes as technical analyst Dark Defender doubled down on his previous $10 XRP prediction, maintaining confidence in the bullish chart structure despite XRP’s recent price weakness.

In a recent post on X, Philion addressed the renewed FUD (fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD) surrounding XRP, arguing that much of the criticism stems from speculation about Ripple’s next moves and what the company may or may not be doing. However, he believes the community has placed too much emphasis on Ripple, creating a misleading perception that XRP’s value and long-term prospects depend on a single corporate player.

“XRP’s value and narrative should never have been perceived as being based solely on the actions of one player,” Philion stated.

The Flare co-founder stressed that XRP has always had greater potential beyond Ripple’s activities, which partly motivated Flare’s creation. In his view, expanding the range of applications available to XRP holders is essential to strengthening the token’s utility, market narrative, and long-term value proposition.

Philion challenged the XRP community to shift its attention toward three fundamental questions: what holders are doing to put their XRP to work, how they can demonstrate its value to people who have yet to invest, and what steps they are taking to transform the cryptocurrency from a speculative holding into usable capital.

He suggested that answering these questions requires more than simply waiting for Ripple to announce new partnerships, products, or adoption initiatives. Instead, XRP holders and developers must actively contribute to building financial applications and use cases that give the asset greater utility.

Philion specifically pointed to Flare as a way to achieve this goal, arguing that the network offers an opportunity to expand what holders can do with their XRP and help separate the asset’s value proposition from Ripple’s corporate decisions.

The Flare co-founder’s remarks come amid growing frustration among XRP holders over the cryptocurrency’s weak price performance. XRP has shed approximately 51% of its value over the past year, trading at around $1.10 at the time of the report. The prolonged decline has also reignited questions about what could drive the token’s next recovery and whether its prospects are too closely tied to Ripple’s business activities.

The criticism has also extended to Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz, who recently faced questions about XRP’s disappointing performance. Schwartz pushed back against suggestions that he could influence the token’s market value, explaining that his ability to move XRP’s price was extremely limited.

Separately, technical analyst Dark Defender remains confident in his double-digit XRP prediction in a recent X post, insisting that the token’s recent decline has not invalidated his broader technical setup.

“Nothing has changed in the structure,” the analyst opined, pointing to the $1.21 and $1.12 support levels he had identified in his October 25 analysis.

According to Dark Defender, XRP’s latest pullback remains within the price scenario he had already mapped out. Rather than abandoning his bullish outlook, he maintained that the cryptocurrency’s movement toward these support zones does not necessarily signal a breakdown of the structure underpinning his longer-term $10 target.

Dark Defender’s earlier Elliott Wave chart outlined a potential rally toward the $10.1101 region. However, reaching that level would require a dramatic recovery from current prices. At $1.10, XRP would need to surge about 809% to reach $10, while climbing to $10.1101 would require roughly an 819% advance.

Given roughly 63.52 billion XRP in circulation, a $10 valuation would put the cryptocurrency’s market capitalization at around $635.2 billion. Reaching the higher $10.1101 target would push its implied market value to around $642.2 billion.

Reuters reported 6,600 cancellations and 8,600 delays, with further cancellations expected Sunday.

Airline shares fell as investors weighed the disruption and a proposed $50 billion system overhaul.

The FAA nationwide ground stop lasted more than four hours. The fallout, however, could keep U.S. airlines dealing with disrupted schedules through the weekend.

The Federal Aviation Administration reopened U.S. airspace at 8:15 p.m. ET on November 13 after a communications failure disrupted air traffic control centers. But restarting departures didn’t put thousands of displaced aircraft and crews back where they belonged.

The NYSE Arca Airline Index closed lower on Friday as airline shares dropped late in the regular session.

American Airlines, Delta and United also fell between 1% and 2% in after-hours trading. JetBlue lost about 3%, adding pressure as investors assessed the disruption.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said overloaded routers and switches produced inconsistent data across air traffic control centers. The FAA halted departures as a safety precaution.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators had found no evidence of a cyberattack so far.

The ground stop is over, but the recovery isn’t automatic. Aircraft remain out of position, crews face duty-time limits, and passengers must be rebooked.

Airlines could spend days rebuilding schedules. The FAA nationwide ground stop has exposed how one failure in shared infrastructure can disrupt the entire industry.

#5215. Binance Reveals Final Numbers After $6.34 Billion Hack: 100.04% of Shiba Inu (SHIB) Reserves Confirmed

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Binance has published the final results of an unscheduled Proof of Reserves (PoR) report, two weeks after the cryptocurrency exchange lost $6.34 billion in an October hack.

According to Binance, the snapshot was taken on Nov. 12 at 00:00 UTC, and it shows that the exchange fully backs the balances of its clients. Shiba Inu (SHIB) is backed at 100.04%, and the other major assets on the exchange are fully covered as well.

The latest report comes after the Oct. 29 attack, during which hackers stole funds from Binance across ten blockchains in 20 minutes. Among the stolen funds were nearly 500 billion SHIB. After the attack, the exchange took an additional reserve snapshot at Bitcoin block height 975493.

Binance data shows that the net account balances of users stand at 50.67 trillion SHIB, and the exchange holds 50.69 trillion SHIB in its wallets. Of that amount, 50.68 trillion SHIB is held at the addresses of Binance itself, and the remaining 7.46 billion SHIB is held by third-party custodians.

Besides SHIB, the report also shows that the other major cryptocurrencies are fully backed. Compared with the previous check on Nov. 4, the BTC balances of users went up by 0.35% to 687,912 BTC, and the coverage ratio for Bitcoin stands at 100.05%. The ETH balances went up by 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH, and the BNB balances increased by 1.03% to 42.95 million BNB.

Still, the USDT balances of users went down by 3.68% to 24.3 billion USDT. At the same time, the stablecoin has the highest coverage ratio in the report at 104.34%.

Arkham Intelligence data shows that the known wallets of Binance currently hold 58.82 trillion SHIB. That is 5.88% of the total supply of the meme coin, and these tokens are worth $251.16 million. In this context, Binance wallets hold 8.13 trillion SHIB (about $34.7 million) more than the amount shown in the PoR report.

According to Binance, the PoR report only covers the deposits of clients and the coins that the exchange keeps to back them, so the company's own funds are not included in the report. Based on the Arkham data, Binance holds about 16% more SHIB than it owes to its clients.

According to Arkham, Binance is still the third-largest exchange by SHIB holdings. Only the burn address with 410.44 trillion SHIB (or 41.04% of supply), the U.S.-based exchange Coinbase with 74.53 trillion SHIB, and South Korea's Upbit with 64.14 trillion SHIB hold more of the meme coin. Robinhood, Crypto.com and Bithumb come after Binance with 57.12 trillion, 34.95 trillion and 16.74 trillion SHIB, respectively.

Finally, Binance said that the PoR system is still computing the final Merkle Root Hash using zk-SNARKs. After that, users will be able to log into their profiles and check that their balances are included in the overall ledger.

At press time, the price of SHIB stands at $0.00000426.

#5214. Solana Lands Major Wall Street Boost as DTCC Targets 2027 Launch of Tokenized Assets: What It Means for SOL

Wall Street is taking another major step toward blockchain adoption, and Solana (SOL) is emerging as one of the networks positioned to benefit. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the financial infrastructure giant that clears and settles much of the U.S. securities market, plans to bring its tokenization services to Solana in 2027.

The move could open the door to tokenized stocks, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and U.S. Treasuries on the blockchain, marking a significant institutional milestone for Solana. But beyond the headline announcement, the obvious question is what this development could mean for the price of SOL and its long-term investment appeal.

DTCC announced Thursday that it plans to extend its tokenization services to Solana in the second half of 2027. The initiative will connect its DTCC Tokenization Service to the Layer 1 blockchain, enabling eligible securities held by its Depository Trust Company subsidiary to be represented as digital tokens.

BREAKING: @The_DTCC to tokenize custodied assets on Solana. announced plans to connect the DTCC Tokenization Service to Solana, enabling the tokenization of eligible DTC-custodied assets on the network.The integration is planned for the second half of 2027, further advancing… pic.twitter.com/gXszWFgUOX

“DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities,” Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services, said in the announcement.

DTCC’s Tokenization Service went live on October 28, initially operating on the Canton Network and the corporation’s own private blockchain, which is built on the Besu framework. The platform allows eligible participants to convert traditional securities into tokenized assets and redeem them back into their original form, with the digital tokens delivered directly to wallets of their choice. At launch, DTCC also outlined plans to expand its tokenization service to additional blockchain networks in 2027, with Stellar and Circle’s Arc among the platforms also slated for integration.

Solana has been stepping up efforts to attract traditional financial institutions, positioning itself as a blockchain capable of supporting large-scale financial activity. Nick Ducoff, head of institutional growth at the Solana Foundation, recently highlighted this appeal, stating that institutions choose Solana because it already “runs real financial activity at scale.” He added that firms are already issuing assets, settling transactions, and deploying capital on the network, according to a post shared by Solana’s official X account.

The potential opportunity becomes clearer when considering DTCC’s position in the U.S. financial system. Through its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary, the financial infrastructure giant holds approximately $114 trillion in securities on behalf of banks and brokerage firms. Its newly launched tokenization service initially covered 34 eligible securities representing an estimated $30 trillion in potential tokenized assets. However, this figure reflects the value of securities eligible for tokenization, not assets already issued or circulating on blockchain networks.

Bringing even a fraction of this enormous securities market onto Solana could translate into substantial institutional activity and settlement volumes over time. This could create additional opportunities for SOL demand if the token is required for relevant network transactions. Nevertheless, the integration is not expected until the second half of 2027, making the development a potential long-term growth driver rather than an immediate price catalyst. Its ultimate impact will depend on institutional adoption, actual transaction volumes, and whether increased network activity translates into meaningful demand for SOL.

#5210. Important Ethereum (ETH) Bug Might Be Finally Fixed

One of Ethereum's consensus clients has merged a fix for a validator pubkey cache poisoning attack, according to a pull request on GitHub. The patch addresses a vulnerability around the Gloas fork, which could result in some nodes rejecting valid signatures due to a bug in the global pubkey cache.

Gloas is the consensus layer part of the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade.

The issue lies in a mechanism where the client stores validator public keys and their indexes in a global cache.

Technically, deposits that are already finalized should give the same validators on every chain, though it is a different story at the fork boundary.

The attacker needs 3 pending deposits just before the fork. The first one is a large top-up for an existing validator. The other two are new keys: A with builder credentials and B with regular validator credentials.

On the canonical chain, the top-up consumes the balance churn, so A and B are processed after the fork. A becomes a builder, and B takes the next validator index.

On the attacker's side chain, the topped-up validator gets slashed before the fork, and its deposit is skipped. This leads to A being processed earlier, essentially taking B's index.

The buggy cache assumed both chains would produce the same validators and imported A's key globally.

At the fork, affected nodes would reject all valid signatures from B on the canonical chain and fork off.

Realistically, the attack is somewhat complicated, as it needs a slashing at the right moment and a side chain, so it's unlikely to happen by accident.

According to the PR, the fix is to only add keys to the global pubkey cache once their activation eligibility epoch is finalized.

A new HeadPubkeys structure also combines keys from the head state and the global cache, so nodes don't miss keys if the chain finalizes without new blocks.

Whether other consensus clients had a similar issue is yet to be confirmed. In other words, the closer Glamsterdam gets, the more edge cases around the fork boundary developers have to catch.

Following the disbandment of the T3 FCU, TRON and Tether have launched a new initiative to tackle criminal activity in USDT on Tron.

Tron and Tether have formed a strategic partnership with blockchain intelligence platform Chainalysis. The coalition aims to crack down on criminal activity involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the Tron blockchain, according to data Tron CEO Justin Sun shared today.

In a Thursday announcement, Tron, Tether, and Chainalysis formed a digital crime task force (DCTF), a new initiative designed to effectively uncover and clamp down on illicit activity involving USDT on the TRON network.

The DCTF brings together three industry leaders – a stablecoin issuer, a crypto network, and a blockchain intelligence firm – aimed at building investigative capability, with support from global law enforcement authorities. The key driver behind the collaboration is to better combat illegal USDT transactions on Tron amid a surge in AI-enabled crime.

The DCTF takes effect after the T3 Financial Crime Unit (T3 FCU), formed by Tether, Tron, and TRM Labs, ended its role in August. The T3 FCU program, which was rolled out in September 2024, was tasked with disrupting unlawful USDT activity on Tron. Its track record has been good. By mid-2025, it had blocked around $250 million in illicit USDT assets, and by May 2026, it had also frozen over $450 million. It had collaborated with law enforcement agencies in 23 jurisdictions.

In the new announcement issued today, Tether and Tron have launched a new initiative to make the crackdown more efficient with Chainalysis’ support. With the recent massive Binance hack, the timing of the fresh partnership is critical.

The Binance exploit highlights serious security risks for crypto platforms. Reports indicate that the hacker sold around $325 million USDT to market makers within minutes of obtaining the stolen funds.

#5204. 15 Years Since David Schwartz First Coded XRP Ledger’s Foundation, XRPL’s First Step?

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011, by David Schwartz.

According to the official XRP account on X, the date 11/11/11 marked the beginning of Schwartz's work on what would later support one of the cryptocurrency industry's established payment-focused blockchain networks.

Schwartz, now Ripple CTO Emeritus, was one of three engineers, alongside Jed McCaleb and Arthur Britto, who began developing the XRP Ledger in 2011. The three were inspired by Bitcoin to build an alternative that would address some of its problems, especially in the areas of sustainability and payments.

In June 2012, the XRP Ledger went live. Shortly after Chris Larsen joined the group in September 2012, a company called NewCoin was formed; it soon changed its name to OpenCoin before becoming Ripple. The founders of the XRPL donated 80 billion XRP, the network’s native digital asset, to the company.

Ripple has locked up most of its XRP in escrow, about 55 billion XRP, and releases 1 billion XRP on the first day of every month.

The anniversary on November 11 marks the start of the XRP Ledger’s development, as what began with Schwartz's first code in 2011 eventually morphed into a blockchain network designed to enable value transfers.

November is also a big month for XRP as U.S. spot XRP ETFs celebrate the first anniversary of their landmark launch.Canary Capital’s XRP exchange-traded fund, listed under the ticker XRPC, began trading on November 13, 2025, and is the first spot XRP ETF on a U.S. exchange.

In upgrade news, XRPL version 3.5.0 is scheduled for December 3, 2026. This release includes only improvements and fixes, including a permanent fix for occasional slow ledger close times.

#5203. Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

#5202. Bitcoin Crash Coming? Analyst Revisits 2014, 2018, and 2022 Pattern Ahead Of Midterm Elections

Bitcoin (BTC) could face another significant correction as the November 3 U.S. midterm elections approach, with analysts pointing to a historical pattern that has coincided with major BTC price declines during previous election cycles.

With the 2026 midterm elections just days away, market observers are examining Bitcoin’s performance around the 2014, 2018, and 2022 elections to see whether another downturn is approaching.

Although the historical similarities do not establish that elections directly influence cryptocurrency prices, the repeated appearance of major corrections during these periods has raised questions about Bitcoin’s near-term direction.

According to crypto analytics platform Alphractal, Bitcoin was already experiencing bearish conditions before each of the previous three midterm elections. However, selling pressure continued after Election Day, with the cryptocurrency eventually reaching significant cycle lows.

Looking back at the 2014 U.S. midterm elections held on November 4, Bitcoin was already caught in an extended bear market. The cryptocurrency continued declining in the weeks that followed, eventually reaching its cycle bottom in January 2015.

A similar development occurred in 2018. Bitcoin was trading around $6,400 when Americans headed to the polls on November 6. Although the market initially experienced a period of relative stability, BTC subsequently suffered a sharp decline, losing approximately 40% over the following month before establishing its cycle bottom in December.

Meanwhile, during the 2022 election cycle, Bitcoin had already experienced considerable losses by the time the November 8 elections took place. The collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX occurred around the same period, triggering another wave of selling that pushed BTC toward $15,500 and marked the bottom of that market cycle.

According to Alphractal, these three occurrences raise an interesting question about whether Bitcoin’s performance has any meaningful relationship with the U.S. electoral calendar.

The analytics platform emphasized that Bitcoin was already in a bear market ahead of all three elections. Consequently, the subsequent declines could have reflected broader cryptocurrency market conditions and the asset’s four-year cycle rather than the elections themselves.

Additionally, popular analyst Ali Martinez highlighted Bitcoin’s historical performance across four U.S. midterm election cycles.

According to Martinez, BTC recorded significant declines around the 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022 midterm elections, with reported losses of 72%, 65%, 52%, and 27%, respectively.

The analyst considers this repeated downside performance a pattern worth monitoring as another election approaches on November 3.

Furthermore, Martinez pointed to Bitcoin’s fourth-quarter returns during previous midterm election years. His figures show that BTC gained 391% in the fourth quarter of 2010, while the cryptocurrency recorded losses of 16.70% in 2014, 42.16% in 2018, and 14.75% in 2022.

The figures suggest that three of the four election-year fourth quarters ended negatively. However, the 2010 rally stands out as an exception, particularly because Bitcoin was still in its early stages of development.

For the upcoming election, Martinez identified $73,000 as an important price level to watch. He pointed to Bitcoin’s short-term holder cost basis, which represents the average acquisition price of coins held by relatively recent market participants.

According to his assessment, this level could become an important support area if selling pressure increases following the elections. A recovery from that region would potentially strengthen the bullish outlook, while continued weakness could signal further deterioration in market conditions.

Beyond the historical election pattern, technical analyst Crypto Patel has also raised concerns about Bitcoin’s immediate price direction, suggesting another substantial decline is possible.

In a recent market update, the pundit said Bitcoin had already fallen about 12% from his previously identified short-entry area. He explained that his bearish outlook originated from technical chart analysis rather than negative headlines or developments affecting the cryptocurrency industry.

The analyst based his assessment on Smart Money Concepts (SMC), which examines market structure, liquidity movements, and price action to identify potential trading opportunities.

Notably, Patel explained that Bitcoin’s price structure had produced a higher high, leading him to anticipate a subsequent move toward a higher low. He also highlighted the removal of inducement liquidity and a higher-timeframe candle closing below the relevant inducement level as additional bearish signals.

Regarding his latest projections, he identified $66,000 to $62,000 as his potential downside target, provided Bitcoin remains below $81,950.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson says he never promised ADA would rise or overtake Bitcoin.

Hoskinson says investors asking him to boost ADA price are effectively asking him to pump bags.

Cardano’s founder says the network’s original roadmap has now been completed and is self-governing.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has a message for ADA holders, he never promised to make the token rise. While ADA has lost nearly 95% from its 2021 peak, leaving investors waiting for a recovery.

Hoskinson says his job was never to pump ADA’s price, it was to build and decentralize Cardano, and that’s done.

During a 7 November livestream, Hoskinson responded to a viewer who brought up his earlier comments about Cardano possibly becoming the biggest cryptocurrency.

“I never promised that. I said I’d love for it to happen, and I believe that Cardano is a better store of value than Bitcoin is for a variety of reasons.”

He explained that saying something could happen is not the same as promising it.

Also, “I don’t promise price appreciation, or people overturning things. I say it’s absolutely possible.

Hoskinson made it clear that he sees potential for Cardano but does not guarantee higher prices or a bigger market position for ADA.

Meanwhile, ADA has fallen from its 2021 all-time high of $3.099 to around $0.1636, a drop of 94.72%.

The discussion became more direct when Hoskinson addressed investors who expected him to keep supporting ADA’s price.

“So you tell me you want me to pump your bags, and if I don’t, I’m a scammer.”

Hoskinson explained that this expectation would never end. If someone buys ADA at $3 and expects $5, the next investor may buy at $5 and expect $7.

If you stop at five, you cheat the person who bought at five. If you stop at three, you cheat the person who bought at three.

There is no way to win, investors will still accuse him of failing them.

At last, Hoskinson said his main responsibility was not to keep ADA’s price rising but to build the network and make it independent. He said Cardano’s “roadmap is complete,” with planned upgrades having been delivered.

Cardano’s development followed five stages, including Byron, Shelley, Goguen, Basho, and Voltaire. Each upgrade added staking, smart contracts, and better network performance.

The final upgrades gave ADA holders voting rights, with the Plomin hard fork completing the shift to community-led governance in January 2025.

“My job was to build it and decentralize it, I have no power over this ecosystem.”

He added that Cardano is now self-governing and can choose its own leaders without his approval.

While Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana have also come under bearish pressure during November’s broader crypto market sell-off, XRP is taking a particularly brutal beating, leaving investors wondering why the token is underperforming its biggest rivals. According to prominent analyst EGRAG Crypto, the weakness is no coincidence, pointing to three key factors that could explain XRP’s sharper decline and signal why the token may continue struggling as bearish sentiment grips the market.

Crypto analyst EGRAG Crypto has highlighted XRP’s worsening performance against Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) amid November’s broader cryptocurrency market drawdown. In a Nov. 10 post on X, the pundit noted the striking difference in losses since November 4, showing that Ripple’s XRP has suffered the steepest decline among the four major cryptocurrencies.

According to EGRAG Crypto’s figures, XRP has plunged 23.4% since November 4, significantly more than ETH’s 18.2% decline and SOL’s 17% drop. BTC has demonstrated greater resilience, losing just 10.4% over the same period.

The figures raise an important question: Why is XRP bleeding considerably more than its major competitors? EGRAG Crypto has pointed to three possible factors behind the token’s disproportionate weakness, offering a closer look at the selling pressure weighing on the Ripple-linked token.

The first factor is leveraged long liquidations, which EGRAG assigns a 30% probability. According to the analyst, forced liquidations of bullish positions, combined with weak buying demand, could be accelerating XRP’s fall. When leveraged traders are forced to close their positions during a downturn, the resulting selling pressure can trigger further losses and deepen an existing market correction.

The second possibility, which carries a 20% probability, is selling by early XRP holders. EGRAG suggests that longtime investors, often referred to as OGs, could be taking profits and rotating their capital into other cryptocurrencies. Such activity could increase selling pressure on XRP, particularly if large holders decide to reduce their exposure amid uncertain market conditions.

Finally, EGRAG assigns the highest probability, 50%, to what the expert describes as market manipulation or a deliberate liquidity hunt. Under this scenario, sharp price movements could be designed to trigger stop-loss orders and force weaker traders out of their positions before a potential recovery. The analyst believes this could explain why XRP is experiencing disproportionately heavy selling compared with other major cryptocurrencies.

Notably, these percentages represent EGRAG Crypto’s personal probability-based assessment rather than independently verified evidence of the causes behind XRP’s decline.

Beyond identifying the possible reasons behind XRP’s sharper decline, EGRAG Crypto has also highlighted several important price levels that could determine the token’s next move. The analyst identified the $1.00-$1.04 range as a critical stabilization zone, suggesting that holding this area could help XRP establish a floor amid the ongoing selling pressure.

On the upside, EGRAG believes bulls must first reclaim the $1.15 level before targeting $1.25. A recovery above these thresholds could signal improving buying momentum and offer some relief to investors after the recent losses.

Sharing a personal assessment, EGRAG Crypto said the ongoing price action appears more consistent with market manipulation designed to frighten newer investors into selling. However, the analyst raised a bigger question about whale activity, questioning whether deep-pocketed XRP holders are using the downturn to accumulate more tokens or adding to the selling pressure by offloading their holdings.

Ultimately, how whales respond to the current market weakness could offer important clues about XRP’s next direction. If large holders are absorbing the available supply, the sell-off could eventually lose momentum. Conversely, continued whale selling could make an already difficult recovery even harder for the sixth-largest cryptocurrency.

#5194. Here’s why Zcash could remove 50,000 ZEC from its grants treasury

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Zcash [ZEC] community is gearing up to vote on a proposal that could significantly change how ZEC funds its development and distributes newly created tokens. The plan involves removing 50,000 ZEC from the Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) treasury and redirecting its value toward future mining rewards.

That said, Zcash currently allocates 8% of newly issued ZEC to ZCG, which uses the funds to support developers, wallet providers, and other ecosystem projects.

These grants help maintain the infrastructure and software needed to use ZEC. However, rising ZEC prices has increased the value of ZCG’s existing treasury, which has raised concerns that the committee was accumulating more funds than necessary while continuing to receive new token allocations.

However, now, under the new proposal, approximately 55% of ZCG’s treasury (50,000 ZEC) would be removed from circulation within 30 days of activation. Going ahead, its value would be credited to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, introduced through the NU7 upgrade. This, in turn, would gradually return ZEC to the network through future mining rewards.

At the same time, the proposal would also end ZCG’s existing 8% allocation of newly created ZEC. Instead, this share would accumulate in a new Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund until the next halving takes place.

As this happens, the fund would remain inaccessible until a separate proposal establishes withdrawal rules. Lastly, ZCG would retain its remaining treasury to continue funding development, while the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund would remain unchanged.

For those unaware, the revised plan follows ZCG’s 3rd November decision to abandon an earlier proposal, which faced criticism for seeking to redirect approximately 98,000 ZEC from existing assets and future income toward mining rewards.

So, now, the next step is community voting, which is scheduled from 16th November to 30th November. Coinholders and community panels will assess the proposal’s support.

If it receives rough consensus, developers, and miners can work toward implementing it through a future network upgrade called NU7.1. However, there is no confirmed activation date yet.

This coincided with Zcash’s monthly active developer count having nearly doubled over the past two years.

According to Glassnode’s report, around 70% of its active developers have more than one year of experience in crypto development, compared with 58% across the wider industry.

Still, ZEC’s price action was under bearish pressure as it was trading at $986.40 at press time after a drop of 1.4% in the past 24 hours.

This followed a recent report by AMBCrypto wherein ZEC fell by 15.25% and Open Interest also declined 13.4%, indicating weakening speculative demand.

Ethereum’s [ETH] staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high (ATH)  of 36.3%, accounting for more than one-third of ETH’s total circulating supply. Well, the rising staking ratio suggests that an increasing number of ETH holders are choosing to lock up their tokens rather than sell or actively trade them.

This comes as Ethereum’s validator queues show that at press time, 911,938 ETH was waiting to be staked with a 16-day, 7-hour wait. Meanwhile, 264,211 ETH was queued to exit with a 5-day, 16-hour wait, plus a 7-day sweep delay.

Both queues are limited by the same churn rate of 256 per epoch, meaning only a fixed amount of ETH can join or leave each epoch, which is why a big backlog translates into longer waits.

In other words, more people want to stake than unstake right now, but the entry line is slowly shrinking, and exiting takes roughly 12-13 days in total once the sweep delay is included.

This comes as the total ETH staked rose from about 42.1 million ETH (roughly 34.5% of supply) in mid-August to about 44.5 million ETH (around 36.5%) at press time. Since late October the climb has resumed steadily.

Of this, BitMine earned $121.4 million from staking and validation activities, accounting for approximately 97% of its total revenue. By the 8th of November, the largest Ethereum DAT held 6.07 million ETH, of which 5.22 million ETH was staked.

That said, the company also estimates that these holdings could generate around $309 million in annual staking rewards, based on an estimated 2.65% yield and an ETH price of $2,234.

On the other hand, SharpLink has accumulated 31,363 ETH in staking rewards as of 9th November. Its strategy also includes liquid staking through Lido, allowing it to receive wstETH in return for its deposited ETH.

All of this happened while the active validators moved in the opposite direction. As per charts, they held near 900K through mid-September, peaking around 912K. But again, they dropped sharply from mid-September to mid-October, falling to about 815K, and have since drifted down to roughly 807K, with a small additional drop on the last day or two.

However, the price action of ETH trading at $2,042.94 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a 15.5% drop in the past week sparks concern. This comes as Ethereum faces renewed selling pressure after losing its $2,250 support level. However, Vitalik Buterin’s recent push to position ETH as a store of value suggests hope.

#5187. Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

Bitcoin news: BTC hit $67,568 as longs were liquidated. Fear is Extreme, but BTC fell further after 15 of 16 past readings.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 13, the BTC USD price fell as low as $67,568 on Binance as a wave of forced selling wiped out leveraged bets on a rebound. It was the cryptocurrency’s lowest price since August 19.

Bitcoin trades at $68,772, down 6.7% in 24 hours and 9.1% in a week. Ether lost 5.5% and Solana 3.4% on the day.

BREAKING: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 and ETH nears $1,900 as selling pressure accelerates in crypto.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

Bitcoin is trading near $69,200 after another sharp daily decline. The chart shows that BTC has broken below the $75,000–$76,000 support zone, which now represents an important resistance area. The immediate level to watch is around $69,000.

A sustained break below it could expose the $64,000–$65,000 support area, followed by $60,000. On the upside, Bitcoin would need to reclaim $75,000 to signal a potential recovery and improve its short-term outlook.

Bitcoin faces several challenges heading into the next difficulty adjustment. The increase in miner-to-exchange transfers, combined with negative demand indicators, suggests that the market is struggling to attract sufficient buying interest.

Still, the Antpool transfers should not be interpreted as proof of widespread miner capitulation. The data identifies a large movement from one mining pool, but does not establish that the coins were sold.

The upcoming difficulty reduction could improve mining conditions and help struggling operators manage their costs. However, it is unlikely to resolve the broader weakness in Bitcoin demand.

Investors will be watching whether exchange transfers translate into actual selling and whether spot-market buyers return. A recovery in demand would help absorb additional supply and provide a stronger foundation for Bitcoin’s next move.

Japanese tech and fintech conglomerate Rakuten Group is among the institutional holders of a U.S. spot XRP ETF, according to the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Rakuten also holds funds tracking Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana, and these positions were worth roughly $6.42 million combined at the end of the quarter on Sept. 30, 2026.

The filing shows that Rakuten held 6,690 shares of the Bitwise XRP ETF worth $111,255. At press time, the price of XRP stands at $1.03, and the shares of the Bitwise fund trade at $11.51, according to SoSoValue, so the XRP ETF stake of Rakuten is now worth about $77,000.

Rakuten is not the only institutional investor in the new XRP funds, and Raymond James Financial has also disclosed positions in spot XRP ETFs, according to SEC filings.

The largest position of Rakuten is in BlackRock's spot Bitcoin fund, the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, and Rakuten held $5,893,593 worth of its shares at the end of the third quarter. Besides, Rakuten owns $263,632 of the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF and $150,728 of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF.

U.S. rules require any institutional manager holding more than $100 million in U.S. exchange-listed securities to disclose its portfolio every quarter, no matter where it's based. Rakuten Group holds about $1.4 billion in U.S. equities, and most of that amount is in shares of satellite operator AST SpaceMobile. In this context, the crypto ETF positions account for less than 0.5% of the U.S. portfolio of Rakuten.

Rakuten is one of the largest tech companies in Japan. The market capitalization of Rakuten stands at about ¥1.4 trillion ($9 billion), and the annual revenue of the company is more than ¥2.5 trillion ($16 billion).

The Rakuten ecosystem spans more than 70 services, from the Rakuten Ichiba marketplace and carrier Rakuten Mobile to banks and brokerages. According to Rakuten, these services have more than 100 million users in Japan and more than 2.1 billion users worldwide.

The latest filing comes amid outflows from spot XRP ETFs. According to SoSoValue, the funds lost $10.42 million on Nov. 9 and another $7.62 million on Nov. 10, and there were no flows on Nov. 11 and Nov. 12. On Oct. 28, the total net assets of the funds stood at $1.51 billion.

Still, the cumulative net inflow of spot XRP ETFs stands at $1.79 billion, and the total net assets of the funds are $1.16 billion, or 1.77% of the market cap of XRP. Finally, the Bitwise XRP ETF is the largest of the five spot XRP funds, and its net assets stand at $420.29 million, according to SoSoValue.

Coinglass’s Altcoin Season Index had a reading of 42 at press time.

Anything above 75 ordinarily counts as altcoin season. This means that the press time reading still leaned towards Bitcoin.

There’s numbers to back this up too. According to CryptoRank, for instance, Bitcoin was up 16.6% over the last 90 days.

Bitway [BTW] has risen by about 220%, Quant [QNT] went up 184%, Midnight Network [NIGHT] by 172% and Raydium [RAY] by 152%. Stacks and NEAR also doubled on the price charts.

A lot of the big names didn’t even keep up with BTC. Solana [SOL], for instance, went up a measly 10% over the same stretch. Binance Coin [BNB] also rose by 10.6%, and Chainlink [LINK] outdid them… with 12%.

So yes, a few altcoins are having a great run. Most of the rest are just watching Bitcoin ride off into the sunset.

At the time of writing, BTC.D was at 60.9%.

On the weekly chart, that’s a range that’s been narrowing for more than a year. The top of that has been sliding since late 2025. The bottom has been going up from around 57%.

Right now, it’s pushing right against the top.

#5181. Ethlabs Calls for Ethereum Quantum Protection in 2027 as Upgrade Priorities Shift

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Ethlabs proposes quantum readiness in 2027 and plans to withdraw its quick-slots work from Hegotá. Developers still need to agree on the network's priorities.

Ethereum's next upgrade debate is becoming a question of how much engineering effort should move toward long-term security. In a November 11 proposal, Ethlabs argues for making quantum protection and resilience against advanced AI-assisted attacks the priority for 2027.

The practical question is which improvements can share an upgrade without slowing the security work. That trade-off deserves attention even from readers who never run a validator: protocol roadmaps influence the software that wallets, exchanges and applications must eventually support.

Ethlabs distinguishes basic readiness from full performance: keeping Ethereum operational with quantum-safe options is the main objective, while matching full network capacity is the more ambitious goal. Its proposed reshuffle includes withdrawing quick slots from Hegotá and reconsidering work outside that security objective.

This is a contribution to Ethereum's development process. A research group's preferred date does not establish an activation date, and an architectural direction still needs specifications, implementations and testing. The useful evidence from here will be what client teams agree to build and what they can demonstrate together.

NewsBTC's earlier coverage of Ethereum's proposed base-layer reconstruction helps explain why changes to speed, security and account design have become closely connected.

One relevant building block is EIP-8141, the frame-transaction proposal. It would let a transaction contain separate steps for validation, fee approval and execution. The design gives accounts more flexibility over how they authorise activity, including a path away from today's elliptic-curve signatures.

It also provides for key rotation, batched operations and alternative fee payment. Those features matter because a cryptographic migration is easier to manage when an account's identity can survive a change in its authorisation method.

That creates an important implementation question. An upgrade can enable a safer signature scheme, but wallet developers still have to expose it clearly, exchanges have to recognise it, and users need a recovery path that they understand. Flexibility in the protocol only becomes useful protection when the surrounding software makes it usable.

Ethereum's quantum-security overview identifies multiple areas of exposure: ordinary account signatures, validator signatures, data commitments and some proof systems. Each has a different role, so replacing one component would leave other migration work outstanding.

The same overview says present-day quantum computers cannot break Ethereum's cryptography. Preparation is being undertaken because a transition across a large network takes time, while future hardware capability is uncertain. Hash-based approaches are among the routes being researched, with different efficiency and deployment challenges from current systems.

The distinction between a future cryptographic threat and an active compromise is essential. Readers should not interpret a more ambitious research timetable as evidence that current Ethereum accounts have suddenly been broken. NewsBTC has previously examined Justin Drake's view of quantum migration as a broader redesign opportunity.

Our reading is that the proposal's significance lies in resource allocation. Every additional feature creates implementation and review work, while concentrating on security can defer improvements that other users want sooner. Neither choice is costless.

A credible programme therefore needs measurable milestones: working clients, agreement on migration behaviour and evidence about performance under the new cryptography. It also needs a clear account of which guarantees are available at each stage.

For ETH holders, those milestones will be more informative than a calendar target alone. The debate now asks developers to turn an ambitious security objective into a sequence that the wider Ethereum ecosystem can actually deliver.

Stellar (XLM), the blockchain co-founded by Jed McCaleb, has become the leader in daily market cap growth for tokenized real-world asset (RWA) funds, according to Token Terminal data published by the RWA Foundation. Over the 24 hours to Nov. 13, the market cap of tokenized funds on Stellar went up by $44.9 million, and the network surpassed both Ethereum and Solana.

Over the same period, the market cap of tokenized funds on Solana, Ethereum and zkSync Era increased by $29 million, $10.8 million and $3.5 million, respectively.

Stellar is currently the second-largest blockchain for tokenized funds after Ethereum, according to Token Terminal. Over the past year, the RWA market on Stellar has grown roughly sixfold and reached $4.67 billion, according to rwa.xyz. At press time, the price of XLM stands at $0.1476.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Stellar was designed with the requirements of banks and transfer agents in mind. In this context, the compliance tools are built into the base layer of the network, and an issuer can vet investors through trustlines, freeze accounts and claw back assets.

Transactions on Stellar settle in 3 to 5 seconds, and the fees on the network are measured in fractions of a cent. Besides, users can move funds to and from fiat currencies through local providers, which are called anchors on Stellar.

Franklin Templeton's BENJI money market fund has run on Stellar since 2021, and it was the first U.S. mutual fund on a public blockchain.

Today, Spiko, Ondo and WisdomTree are also building their own funds and tokenized U.S. Treasuries on Stellar. Spiko offers euro funds managed by Amundi, and Ondo has launched its USDY token on the network.

In May 2026, DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announced that the Depository Trust Company (DTC) will tokenize the assets it holds in custody on Stellar. According to DTCC, DTC-tokenized assets are expected to become available on the network in the first half of 2027.

On Nov. 12, DTCC also announced that it will connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027.
