BTC has slipped below $70k for the first time since August, as Peter Schiff believes the asset is in a long-term downtrend, with more slumps yet to come.

Bitcoin has seen another slump amid a broader market sell-off, temporarily sinking to $68,000 before rebounding to the $69k level. The asset currently trades at $68,870, down 9.2% over the past week, as massive crypto liquidations hit long positions amid renewed market volatility.

Dropping below the $73k support triggered a second leg down following recent waves of liquidations driven by recent U.S. midterm elections and the Binance hack, which altered market sentiment.

Statistics indicate that this is the first time BTC has plummeted below $70k since August. With the market embracing this downward trajectory, it’s apparent that short sellers have gained control of the bearish momentum. The asset is currently testing the $68k region, and a drop below that support could pave the way toward $65,000.

According to data reported by CryptoQuant, the decline is largely driven by increased selling pressure amid rising anxiety over possible December interest-rate hikes, surging U.S. Treasury yields, U.S. Dollar appreciation, and weakness in AI-related stocks, pushing investor sentiment toward risk aversion.

The Bitcoin Bull Cycle Drawdowns indicator (shared by CryptoQuant) showed that the token is down about 19% from its ATH, surpassing the historical average drop-offs seen in previous bull markets. However, the data showed that as long as the wider bull market structure remains stable, historical drop-off patterns suggest the current price range could be a key area for a possible market bottom.

Meanwhile, American stockbroker Peter Schiff has warned that BTC is in a long-term bear market and its downtrend is far from over. In his post, the renowned economist said the token is retreating below its 2021 ATH of $69k, describing the fall as a key indicator of weakness.

In a crypto podcast aired on Thursday, Schiff cautioned that BTC could crash below $10k, claiming the market could have already hit the ceiling despite the rising political and corporate backing. He said the asset has failed to gain traction despite favorable developments, including President Trump’s support and institutional adoption.

He is convinced that the asset’s failure to surge on positive developments indicates declining demand and could trigger further selling.

#5177. Apex Joins Hedera Council as Fund Servicing Moves Deeper Into Tokenization

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Apex Group has joined Hedera Council. The appointment brings a fund-services specialist into network governance, while its commercial use of Hedera remains an area for exploration.

Apex Group is adding a governance role to its digital-asset work. Hedera's November 11 announcement says the financial-services provider, which services more than $3.5 trillion in assets, has joined the council overseeing the public network.

Apex plans to explore Hedera within its tokenization initiatives, including the infrastructure needed to manage assets and coordinate settlement. The assets-serviced figure describes the scale of Apex's broader business; it is not a measure of assets committed to this network.

The appointment puts a firm familiar with running financial products inside the network's decision-making structure. That experience can matter because a tokenized fund needs much more than a token-creation tool. Someone must maintain investor records, process subscriptions and redemptions, apply transfer restrictions and explain how the digital record connects to legal ownership.

Our reading is that this is the more useful way to assess the news. A governance appointment can improve the conversation about institutional requirements, but the commercial result will depend on the products and workflows that follow.

NewsBTC's report on Solana's delivery-versus-payment infrastructure explores a related operational problem: coordinating the asset and cash sides of a transaction.

The Hedera Council's governance FAQ describes a structure with up to 39 members, each holding one vote. Responsibilities include decisions on network pricing, software updates and treasury management, alongside participation in governance transactions and operation of a network node.

Membership is a governance interest. It does not give a member ownership of treasury HBAR or an entitlement to distributions from the council. The rules also say members are not required to build applications on Hedera.

Those details help separate two kinds of commitment. Apex has entered the governance structure; a particular fund deployment, transaction volume or tokenization mandate needs its own evidence. HBAR investors should be able to follow each development without having to infer a commercial contract from a council announcement.

A separate April 2025 announcement from Tokeny documented its partnership with the then-named HBAR Foundation to bring regulated asset-tokenization technology to Hedera. That work focused on ERC-3643, a token standard designed around identity and transfer controls.

Tokeny described two integration routes: institutions could use its platform or connect its APIs to existing systems. The practical significance is that an issuer can keep established operational processes while adding blockchain functions, rather than rebuilding every part of fund administration at once.

This earlier work is background to the current governance news. It shows that infrastructure development and institutional engagement have been progressing through separate steps. It does not establish that every prospective use case has reached production.

For a fund administrator, a useful tokenized product should make an existing task easier to execute, reconcile or audit. The meaningful questions are therefore concrete: which assets are supported, which investors qualify, how transfer restrictions are enforced and how exceptions are resolved.

The same implementation challenge appears in NewsBTC's coverage of Chainlink's cross-chain dividend demonstration. Moving a financial asset onto a ledger leaves the ongoing obligations attached to that asset intact.

Apex's council seat gives it a role in shaping the infrastructure. The next evidence to watch is named deployments with defined servicing arrangements and measurable activity. That will show how far governance participation translates into financial products that clients use.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

#5175. Bitcoin volatility falls to 45% – Here’s what it does NOT mean for BTC

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Crypto evaluation, especially for Bitcoin [BTC], tends to be shifting from highly volatile to a mature asset. Bitcoin volatility has fallen to 45% over its 18 years of existence, within the range of common large-cap U.S. stocks.

For instance, JPMorgan and Amazon are at 80% and 90%, respectively, meaning they are a bit more volatile than BTC. Oracle, Coinbase, Micron, and Sandisk are more stable, with their volatilities well below 20%.

This current reading of Bitcoin volatility reflects an asset that has matured with greater institutional participation. However, this does not mean that BTC is now a low-risk asset.

Therefore, the asset deserves another risk framework different from how it was viewed in the past 10 years. During its initial stages, the volatility was exceeding 100% against a capitalization of single-digit billions.

Interestingly, during periods of strong positive momentum, Bitcoin’s gains were achieved faster than the downside deviation as per the Sortino ratio. Still, that does not negate sudden and more aggressive nosedives.

Therefore, maturity has been driven by clearer regulations, more secure investment vehicles like ETFs, and institutional involvement. BlackRock, Grayscale, Strategy, and Morgan Stanley are a few of the deeply involved institutions in BTC adoption.

The maturity of Bitcoin has created opportunities for a more diversified crypto portfolio. Other crypto sectors are becoming less tied to Bitcoin’s price performance, an edge ahead of traditional assets.

Most traditional assets are related to one another.

For instance, the annualized volatility of Smart Contracts Platforms is at 58%, with BTC contributing 38% while sector-specific drive was 20%.

However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) was at 85%, probably because it was somehow new in the financial markets. For this, Bitcoin-driven volatility was 35%, while sector-specific was 50%.

Events like the resignation of the CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, after having an affair with a Chinese spy, have greatly impacted the AI market sector.

Other sectors in crypto, like financials, are at 59%, with 30% being Bitcoin-driven. This phenomenon is quite evident with seasonality in the crypto market.

But Bitcoin seasons are characterized by selective altcoin performance. On the other hand, altcoin seasons have BTC being performed by more than 75 alts in the top 100 by capitalization. Currently, only 45 altcoins have performed better than Bitcoin in the past 90 days.

All in all, crypto maturity is not only on Bitcoin but also in the whole sector. Therefore, a crypto risk framework should be done across more than one dimension to reflect its evolution.

#5174. Solana Company Reports $3.4M Quarterly Revenue as Staking Business Expands

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Solana Company reported $3.4 million in third-quarter revenue, mostly from staking. Its results show how validator operations can add an operating business to a corporate SOL treasury.

Solana Company is beginning to report more of the economics behind its infrastructure strategy. In its November 11 earnings release, the Nasdaq-listed company said revenue reached $3.4 million in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $697,000 a year earlier.

The question for shareholders is how much of that business can grow beyond the size of the company's own token holdings. A balance sheet gives exposure to SOL; an operating validator business adds a different set of customers, costs and performance measures.

The company reported approximately 2.4 million SOL across its holdings categories at quarter-end. It earned 30,800 SOL in quarterly staking rewards and restaked them. Its Pacific Backbone infrastructure had about 1.3 million SOL delegated, including roughly one million from third parties.

Those figures describe different relationships with tokens. Treasury assets belong to the company, while third-party delegations represent outside stake using its infrastructure. Combining the two into a single ownership figure would overstate the company's treasury.

NewsBTC's coverage of DeFi Development Corp's SOL accumulation provides useful context on the distinction between growing a token balance and creating value for each share.

The company's February infrastructure roadmap set out plans to connect Seoul, Tokyo, Singapore and Hong Kong through a low-latency validator network. Its intended customers included trading firms, exchanges and institutional partners.

The stated business logic was to bring more infrastructure work in-house while developing services that outside customers could use. That provides a useful baseline for judging the latest update: the original plan involved building an activity that could generate fees as well as supporting treasury staking.

The programme also envisaged additional liquidity and execution services. Those earlier ambitions should be assessed separately from what subsequent financial reports demonstrate. A roadmap is useful for tracking delivery, but it cannot substitute for revenue, customers and operating margins.

Solana's official staking documentation explains that token holders delegate stake to validators that process transactions and participate in running the network. Validators may retain a commission from rewards to cover their work and costs.

This structure creates two routes to an operating benefit. A company can earn rewards on its own delegated tokens, and a validator operator can earn commissions for serving other holders. The economics depend on performance, expenses and the amount of stake retained.

The documentation also makes a useful accounting distinction: staking increases are measured in SOL units. Their value in dollars moves with SOL's market price. More tokens therefore do not automatically mean a higher fiat value at the end of a reporting period.

Our assessment is that third-party delegation makes the business more interesting to analyse, because it introduces demand from customers outside the treasury. It also makes the reporting more demanding. Investors need to distinguish rewards earned on company assets from fees earned on client stake and then compare both with operating costs.

Capital structure remains important. Issuing shares can expand a treasury while changing the amount of token exposure attributable to each shareholder. Cash expenses can also require financing even when reported token holdings rise.

Custody and access are additional parts of the picture, as NewsBTC examined in Solmate's disclosure of its SOL custody arrangements. Subsequent reports showing delegation retention, fee income and cash expenditure will help establish whether Solana Company's infrastructure adds durable earnings alongside its asset exposure.

#5173. Russia Legalizes Crypto Trading While XRP Stands Apart

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Russia Legalizes Crypto Trading While XRP Stands Apart

Platforms are able to conduct business operations in crypto, offering retail knowledge-based accessibility.

Russia’s crypto bid is going at a faster pace since the fourth largest economy around the globe introduced crypto trading for retail & businesses. The new set of rules, coming from the Central Bank Of Russia, limits regular investors to a 300,000 rubles yearly cap (roughly $3,600).

This allows buying & holding Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) & USDT through regulated intermediaries (brokers, trust managers & licensed exchanges). Everyone must pass a knowledge test plus review risk disclosures before starting trading activities, while XRP is considered an asset for advanced users only.

The Moscow Exchange already lists cash-settled perpetual futures (XRP/USDF) and related indices tracking XRP prices. These are available only to qualified investors, settle in rubles (no actual XRP is delivered), and form part of a broader set of crypto derivatives with substantial turnover among Futures traders across the scene.

Russian Central Bank: Exchanges May Conduct Crypto Trading from November 22, Subject to Prior Approval of Trading Rules According to TASS, the Bank of Russia said Russian exchanges may begin offering cryptocurrency trading from November 22, 2026, provided they first agree on… pic.twitter.com/txoYyq5vfL

The fresh legal framework dates back to August. Then, Russia’s President Vladimir Putin signed the inaugural comprehensive cryptocurrency law (Federal Law No. 282-FZ, “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights”), setting September 1, 2026 activation window: contrastingly to the entry-level investor restrictions, qualified ones have no limits.

Meanwhile, businesses face hard limits, needing to meet a minimum equity requirement (15 million rubles, roughly $187,000) to run crypto services or custody services. The regulatory framework is way more lenient on businesses conducting cross-border sanctions to dodge the 21-chapter European Union sanction packages.

The retail crypto trading gets legalized on November 22, 2026, the related Duma documents state. The approved exchanges & crypto brokers are obliged to report the trading data and results to the central bank in accordance with existing reporting procedures for XRP & others.

For XRP traders in the region, the MOEX XRP Futures index allows up to 5x leverage.

RUSSIA MADE A MASSIVE $XRP MOVE!! pic.twitter.com/dmuUaPnsuP

Paying with XRP or any other popular crypto coin at a local store is still off the table. Goods & services are prohibited as a result of a separate ban, pushing crypto adoption in the perspective of an investment vehicle rather than a means of payment.

Still, setting up state-surveilled crypto brokers is a pretty big move that could inspire other major economies to do the same.

Trezor confirmed on the 12th of November that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis contained malicious implants. Fortunately, no customer had reported losing funds.

Still, Trezor urged affected buyers to move their crypto after releasing a firmware fix.

Customers bought those 3 devices between the 20th of August and the 23rd of September through CryptoBilis directly or its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined one device in its lab and identified two more from customer photos.

The hardware wallet company also urged those using its devices to move funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. It told buyers with unused devices to leave them unconfigured. Eligible buyers could contact Trezor Support for a replacement or a refund where shipping limited their options.

Trezor dropped CryptoBilis on the 9th of October after reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through them. A customer also flagged a suspected Safe 5 implant on the 28th of October.

#5170. Aave Proposal Targets $3.5M in Added Annual Revenue Through Reserve-Factor Changes

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: TokenLogic proposes changes to Aave's reserve factors across 54 reserves. Its model estimates $3.5 million in additional annual revenue, using November 9 balances and rates; governance has not yet approved the changes.

Aave's latest revenue proposal focuses on how lending income is divided. A November 12 submission from TokenLogic covers 12 V3 instances and V2 Ethereum, with the modeled blended reserve factor rising from 12.0% to 12.7%.

The practical issue is straightforward: the protocol treasury would retain a larger share of interest, leaving a smaller share for suppliers where a change applies. Whether that improves the economics over time depends partly on how those suppliers respond.

Aave's official FAQ defines the reserve factor as the percentage of borrowing interest that accrues to the treasury. It is set for each asset through governance. The treasury is controlled by Aave Governance, rather than functioning as a conventional company's bank account.

A simplified example makes the mechanism clearer. Suppose borrowers generate $100 of interest and a reserve factor is 20%. Before considering other mechanics, $20 goes to the treasury and $80 remains for suppliers. Raising the factor to 25% changes that split to $25 and $75. The underlying $100 of interest has not grown simply because the allocation changed.

This hypothetical illustrates why a higher reserve factor can improve treasury receipts while reducing the attractiveness of supplying to the same market. It also shows why the percentage should not be read as an annual return paid to either group.

TokenLogic proposes moving Ethereum Core DAI's factor from 25% to 30%, while Avalanche V3 USDC would move from 10% to 25%. The proposal's stated purpose includes changing incentives across legacy markets as Aave's newer infrastructure develops.

The immediate parameter change does not itself alter the borrower interest rate. Over time, however, a supplier response could change available liquidity and utilisation. Those subsequent effects make it important to distinguish a mechanical estimate from a forecast of the eventual outcome.

NewsBTC's report on Aave's externally curated V4 markets offers context on how the protocol is developing different arrangements for managing liquidity and risk.

Aave's official protocol changelog records the launch of V4 on Ethereum in March and on Avalanche in July. The architecture groups liquidity into hubs and lending activity into separate spokes, giving the network a different way to organise markets.

That deployment history helps explain why comparisons between versions now matter commercially. A supplier considering a change in yield can compare not only competing protocols but also different Aave deployments, with their own assets, liquidity conditions and operational characteristics.

Our reading is that governance is making an allocation decision about where activity should be encouraged. That deserves scrutiny at the individual-market level: a portfolio-wide revenue estimate can hide quite different experiences for suppliers of different assets.

The revenue figure annualises a snapshot. Borrowed balances can rise or fall, interest rates can change, and liquidity can move after a parameter update. The estimate therefore gives a basis for comparison, while the realised result remains open.

Governance also has to consider the cost of retaining liquidity and the resilience of each market. An extra dollar of treasury income is less useful if the settings create an offsetting loss of activity or a more fragile funding base.

Interest in AAVE ownership, including Payward's recently disclosed investment, makes these economic decisions relevant to a wider audience. The next steps are community feedback and an onchain proposal, followed by measurable results if the changes are approved and executed.

#5169. Strategy Sends Crucial Message on Bitcoin's Quantum Security

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an important message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

Saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of new cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin users moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing issue.

One of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

#5166. Binance Halts Luna Classic Burns: What’s Going On?

Home » Altcoins » Binance Halts Luna Classic Burns: What’s Going On?

Terra Luna Classic’s community got used to the monthly burning ceremonies, but this time it’s postponed.

A few weeks after Binance’s $6.4 billion hack following an employee’s laptop breach, the largest digital asset exchange across the globe is resuming most of their regular services. However, the Terra Luna Classic (LUNC) community has missed the monthly LUNC burn, coming from 50% of fees garnered from Binance’s LUNC-related trading pairs.

Typically done on the first of the month, this time Binance’s LUNC burn didn’t arrive at all, chain records show. That’s the first break in a pattern running since March 2023, when Binance pledged to help restore the downtrodden Terra Luna Classic community’s hope in LUNC’s long-term restoration efforts via continuous token burns.

On-chain records show 50 batches of LUNC burns being carried out by Binance on an earlier note. The last one, which was on October 1, 2026, eliminated 335 million tokens, pushing the exchange’s cumulative Terra Luna Classic burn count towards 91 billion.

That’s roughly 19.6% of all LUNC burns to this date, a considerable contribution in the deflationary campaign.

Still no statement from @Binance regarding the monthly #LUNC burn.. Although we understand the massive hack, I feel as though a statement should at least be made to #LunaClassic investors. Is this a temporary pause or indefinite?.. pic.twitter.com/Od2yH1kFgn

Some LUNC community members are floating the main reason for the delay to be apparent changes in wallet security, but Binance confirmed no such action. Naturally, the internal wallet reshuffling can be a normal practice following the multi-billion dollar hack and the day-by-day withdrawal restoration efforts done with diligence.

Back in August, the community behind Terra Luna Classic revisited the proposal 12223 to raise the on-chain transaction tax to 1.5%. Of that, 1.2 percentage points go towards burning even more LUNC coins. Meanwhile, strong voices in the crypto community have been advocating for more exchanges beyond Binance to burn fixed-fee allocations.

KuCoin & OKX were among the ones named in negotiations. The game-tested altcoin still has a massively over-minted supply of 5.5 trillion tokens in circulation, a figure normally ascribed to meme coins.

The feature addresses a practical obstacle for public-ledger payments. A business may want the settlement benefits of a blockchain without publishing every payment amount to competitors or employees. Individual users can have similar concerns about exposing the size and history of their financial activity.

The technical documentation separates confidentiality from anonymity. In the default confidential ring, assets, amounts and optional memos are encrypted during private transfers, while the participating wallet addresses remain public. A visible transaction hash also remains part of the record.

Entering from a public balance has a different footprint: the deposit's asset, amount and addresses are visible, even though the resulting private balance is encrypted. Users should therefore understand each step of a payment, rather than assume that selecting a private balance hides all earlier activity.

This is a meaningful improvement for applications that mainly need to conceal amounts. It also establishes a clear limit: a counterparty relationship can still be observable. Product designers will need to explain that distinction before users rely on it.

Helius says developers can integrate the system through APIs and build private escrows for financial activity. Its planned uses include confidential swaps, staking and yield-related applications. The launch provides a foundation that other teams can incorporate into their products.

The broader usability question also appears in NewsBTC's reporting on Samsung Wallet's live USDC rollout on Solana. Reaching users requires a workable product around the underlying network capability.

The foundation says the enterprise version is expected in the coming weeks. That expectation should be tracked as a delivery milestone. The current permissionless launch and the planned enterprise release have different operating requirements.

For an institution, confidentiality is only one part of the problem. Staff still need appropriate access, auditors need reliable evidence, and a payment's legal and accounting treatment must remain clear. NewsBTC's coverage of Solana's delivery-versus-payment programme examines another piece of that wider settlement workflow.

The foundation reports audits of the core programmes and proof circuits by Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security, while formal verification is still underway. It also identifies applications and service providers working with the infrastructure. These are useful implementation details, with separate questions still open about usage and long-term reliability.

#5163. Chainlink and Moody’s Complete Testnet Pilot for Cross-Chain Credit Ratings

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainlink and Moody's Ratings completed a cross-chain distribution pilot using test data. It ran on testnets and did not publish live rating actions or change Moody's existing publication processes.

Tokenized finance needs information to move alongside assets. In a November 10 announcement, Chainlink and Moody's Ratings reported a completed pilot that used the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, to distribute credit information across multiple networks.

The exercise connected Moody's Token Integration Engine, known as TIE, with cross-chain messaging. Its significance lies in a familiar market problem: investors need consistent information about an instrument even when different pieces of financial infrastructure represent or hold it.

The pilot used representative data in a controlled testnet environment, spanning permissioned and permissionless networks. No actual rating actions were published onchain, and live dissemination processes were not involved.

That scope makes the result useful as an interoperability test. It leaves the separate work of operating a production service, setting responsibilities and integrating it with financial institutions.

Consider a hypothetical bond represented across several networks. If its credit assessment changes, a reliable system needs to identify the relevant instrument and ensure each destination receives the appropriate update. Otherwise, applications can act on different versions of information about the same underlying obligation.

Chainlink's documentation describes CCIP as infrastructure for transferring both data and tokens between blockchains. Its developer tools cover standalone messages and transactions that combine value transfers with instructions.

This matters because a rating update is information. Delivering it does not necessarily require moving the asset itself. A recipient application can receive a message and decide how to use it according to its own rules and permissions.

The documentation also includes message-status, execution and finality tools. Those operational details become important when a financial workflow needs to determine whether an update has arrived, whether it has been processed and how to handle an exception.

NewsBTC has examined the configurable controls around this infrastructure in its report on CCIP 2.0's security and compliance features.

The new test sits within a longer programme. In June, Moody's announced an Alphaledger integration for Solana, giving issuers on that platform an option to integrate ratings with tokenized fixed-income assets. That followed TIE's March deployment on Canton.

Moody's described TIE as network-agnostic. The aim is to make its analytical information available within different blockchain environments, with the underlying credit opinion retaining its established role.

This history is useful because connecting a ratings service to one network and distributing information across several networks are related but separate tasks. The latest pilot tests a way to extend that reach; it should not be presented as the first time Moody's explored blockchain delivery.

Our assessment is that the hardest questions extend beyond whether a message can cross a network boundary. A production workflow needs clear instrument identifiers, controls over who can publish updates, a record of changes and rules for handling delayed or disputed information.

It also needs to preserve the meaning of the data. A credit rating is an analytical opinion about credit risk. Putting that opinion onchain does not make an asset risk-free or remove the need to assess its liquidity, price and legal terms.

Similar lifecycle work appears in NewsBTC's coverage of Chainlink's tokenized-equity dividend demonstration. A ledger can carry an asset, but the asset's obligations and information still need maintenance.

The pilot offers evidence that one distribution route can work in a test setting. Named production integrations, defined update policies and operating records would provide the next evidence of how it performs for real portfolios.

#5161. Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

Home » Regulations » Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

A $10.8 trillion payroll tax gap is accelerating Social Security’s 2032 shortfall—and reshaping retirement and investment strategies.

For years, the impending Social Security funding crunch has been framed as a simple demographic math problem: Baby Boomers are retiring faster than younger workers can replace them.

While an aging population plays a role, a new economic analysis reveals a far bigger, largely overlooked culprit—a structural shift in how U.S. income is earned and taxed that has quietly starved the program of $10.8 trillion and shaved a quarter-century off its solvency timeline.

According to a November 2026 study from the AARP Public Policy Institute, the program’s trust funds could have paid 100% of scheduled benefits until 2059 if the share of the U.S. economy subject to payroll taxes had simply held steady at 1983 levels.

Instead, the retirement fund is projected to deplete its reserves in late 2032, putting millions of Americans on track for automatic Social Security cuts exceeding $500 a month.

Social Security relies on payroll taxes for roughly 91% of its annual funding, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report. However, a shrinking slice of U.S. economic output comes from traditional wages covered by that tax.

AARP’s analysis found that wages subject to Social Security payroll taxes accounted for 41% of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) in 1983. By 2025, that share had fallen to 34%. That 7% represents an estimated $10.8 trillion in lost tax revenue and interest between 1984 and 2034.

The report attributes this erosion to several modern economic shifts:

Under current projections from the Social Security Administration, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) trust fund, which pays retirement and survivor benefits, will run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress were to merge it with the separate Disability Insurance trust fund, combined reserves would last until 2034.

Depletion does not mean Social Security payments will stop entirely, because active workers will continue paying payroll taxes into the system. However, without legislative action, incoming tax revenue will only cover 78% of scheduled retirement benefits in 2032 (or 83% on a combined basis in 2034).

That translates to an automatic 22% across-the-board cut in 2032—reducing the average retiree’s monthly check by more than $500 in over half of U.S. states.

With less than six years before the 2032 deadline, lawmakers face a narrow window to either broaden how the program captures revenue from a shifting economy or let an automatic benefit reduction take effect by default.

A 22% reduction in Social Security payouts would directly compress disposable income for tens of millions of U.S. households, reshaping consumer spending, personal savings rates, and long-term fiscal deficit projections.

First, concerns about the long-term future of Social Security could lead some younger Americans to take more responsibility for their own retirement savings. For some investors, that may mean looking beyond traditional retirement accounts to alternative assets, including Bitcoin and crypto ETFs.

Second, proposals to strengthen Social Security by taxing a broader range of income could have implications for financial markets. If lawmakers eventually target investment income or adjust capital gains taxes, the changes could affect investor behavior and market liquidity across both traditional and digital asset markets.

On the 12th of November, TRON, Tether, and blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis jointly launched the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF), an initiative aimed at identifying and disrupting illicit financial activities involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain.

In this plan, TRON will contribute its blockchain network expertise, and Tether will provide support as the issuer of USDT. Meanwhile, Chainalysis will bring its blockchain intelligence, investigative expertise, and AI-powered monitoring tools.

One of the major reasons behind the initiative is the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime. According to Chainalysis, AI-enabled scam operations were 4.5x more profitable than traditional scams in 2025. Meanwhile, impersonation scams increased by more than 1,400% year over year.

DefiLlama further reported that the crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026 so far. This is the highest annual loss recorded in its database. In fact, the five biggest hacks together contributed more than 85% of the overall losses.

Interestingly, the number of attacks increased around 2.7 times compared to 2025, while the median loss declined from $1.07 million to $510,000. This suggests that hackers are carrying out more frequent attacks, although most incidents involve relatively smaller amounts.

Seeing this rise, the organizations believe that traditional approaches, which often depend on victims reporting crimes or investigators identifying suspicious funds, are no longer sufficient. Instead, they want to identify potential threats before criminals can move their funds.

Remarking on the same, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said,

Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

This remark comes as Tether has already frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activities while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

That said, the new task force will therefore be built on these efforts by focusing on proactive investigations and faster coordination. It will also accept tips and asset-freezing requests directly from law enforcement agencies.

Needless to say, the DCTF will investigate several categories of financial crime, including investment and romance scams, stolen funds, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, and much more.

This coincided with the FBI recently launching ‘Operation Blackout,’ a coordinated international crackdown targeting scam compounds across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East that defraud American citizens through fake investment platforms and online impersonation.

Meanwhile, ACAMS has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to strengthen cryptocurrency anti-financial crime training through an updated CCAS certification.

#5159. What Are Solana Privacy Rings? Inside Helius’ Privacy Protocol for Solana

Every transaction on Solana is public by default. Anyone can look up a wallet address and see its balance, what it has sent and received, and when. That transparency is useful for verifying the network, but a problem for anyone who doesn't want their finances on display: a business paying salaries, a trader building a position, or an individual who simply doesn't want strangers seeing their savings.

Rings are programmable, onchain environments for encrypting money, markets, and finance - without ever leaving Solana

Now live on mainnet. pic.twitter.com/ezCIUCjcbI

Rings support SOL and other tokens on Solana, including SPL and Token-2022 tokens. Users keep custody of their funds throughout, since every transaction needs the owner's signature.

Crucially, the private balances live on the same network as everything else. Private transactions execute directly on Solana and encrypted data is stored on Solana's ledger, with no separate layer-2 network or sequencer in between. That means private balances sit alongside the same stablecoins, tokenized assets and DeFi liquidity as public ones.

Each private transfer comes with a zero-knowledge proof, a piece of cryptography that lets the network confirm the transfer is valid, for example that the sender actually had the funds, without revealing the numbers involved. Rings use a type of zero-knowledge proof called a Groth16 zk-SNARK, which Helius says can be generated in tens of milliseconds, either by a service provider or on the user's own device. Each private transfer settles in a single Solana transaction.

Users read their own encrypted balances with a viewing key. They can decrypt their balance locally, or let a service provider decrypt it and serve it to them, and they can share a key for a single transaction with an auditor or counterparty without exposing the rest of their history.

Moving funds into a Ring from an ordinary public wallet, or back out again, is visible onchain, including the asset and amount. But users who on-ramp from fiat currency straight into a private balance, through a supported provider, keep the asset and amount hidden from the start, according to Helius.

Because Custom Rings interoperate with the default Ring, regulated firms can keep their activity confidential from the market while still sharing the same liquidity as everyone else.

Private transfers are just the start. Solana programs can hold encrypted balances in private escrows and release them when set conditions are met, opening the way for:

At launch, Decrypt, mining and staking app ORE and cross-chain service Aurora Intents were using the default Ring, while Backpack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan were among the teams working on integrations.

Helius says the core programs and zero-knowledge circuits have been audited by security firms Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security. Engineers from the Solana Foundation, Blueshift, Zcash and other teams took part in the "trusted setup," the one-off ceremony that generates the parameters the proofs rely on.

The code is open source, published on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, so anyone can inspect how it works.

Formal verification, a mathematical check that the circuits behave exactly as intended, is still underway and expected to finish by the end of 2026. Solana's own documentation currently describes Rings as being in beta.

#5158. Sygnum Launches ETH Fund Targeting 8–10% Returns in Ether

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Sygnum has announced an ETH-denominated fund targeting 8–10% annual returns after fees. The target includes staking income, and investors remain exposed to ETH's market price.

Sygnum is pitching a different measure of investment performance: how much Ether an investor owns at the end of the year. In its November 12 announcement, the bank introduced the ETH Alpha Fund, which opened to investors on November 2 and is aimed at professional and qualified investors in approved markets.

The fund's product page makes two distinctions explicit. Its 8–10% objective is the total portfolio target, including staking. It is also denominated in ETH, so the value of an investment in dollars or another currency continues to move with Ether's price.

That changes how the headline number should be read. As a hypothetical illustration, an investor starting with 100 ETH and achieving an 8% token return would finish with 108 ETH. If the dollar price of Ether fell 20% over the same period, the position's dollar value would still be 13.6% lower.

That example describes arithmetic, not a forecast for the fund. It shows why increasing a token balance and preserving purchasing power are different objectives. The meaning of a successful year depends on which currency the investor uses to measure it.

Sygnum says the portfolio combines native staking with options premiums, arbitrage and derivatives carry or funding strategies. The trading component aims to earn returns without relying on a directional call on ETH.

Ethereum's staking documentation explains the underlying distinction. Validators receive rewards for their role in maintaining the network. They can also lose ETH through inactivity penalties or slashing, while using a service provider adds another counterparty to the arrangement.

Trading income has a separate economic source. An options premium compensates the seller for accepting an obligation; an arbitrage strategy depends on a pricing difference that can be captured after costs. Neither is simply an extra protocol reward.

Combining these activities may diversify the sources of income. It also makes the resulting product more complex to evaluate than a straightforward staking position.

The launch announcement says trading uses Sygnum Protect, keeping collateral off exchanges at the bank. The product page lists a minimum subscription of $100,000 or its ETH equivalent, monthly subscriptions and monthly redemptions, with advance notice requirements. It also lists an investor-level gate of up to 10%, although the page does not explain its mechanics.

Those terms matter for an institution that must meet cash demands on a different timetable. A quoted asset value does not necessarily mean that capital can be withdrawn immediately. A treasury evaluating such a structure has to match its investment horizon with the fund's dealing arrangements.

Custody deserves the same attention. NewsBTC's coverage of Sygnum's MultiSYG lending arrangement illustrates how the control of collateral can be designed separately from the financial exposure attached to it.

This launch sits within the broader expansion of institutional ETH products, alongside developments such as Amundi's Ethereum-based fund share class. The products serve different purposes, even though both use Ethereum-related infrastructure.

For the new fund, the useful evidence will be realised returns, the consistency of those returns and how its strategies behave when market conditions change. Comparisons also need the same accounting basis: net with net, ETH with ETH and equivalent observation periods.

An annual target gives investors an objective to assess. A live track record will show how closely the fund can follow it.

Most altcoins did not see any spikes in selling because they were already oversold. SHIB does not show a very strong correlation with Bitcoin; rather, it correlates with altcoins of the same echelon, so a recovery will be possible on par with the broader market retrace that would include assets like XLM, XRP and Ethereum.

The market is weak and might get weaker, but the most selling pressure SHIB could face has already been injected.

Shiba Inu volumes are extremely low, which suggests a lack of volatility ahead. It is also a good sign for a bearish market.

#5156. Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

On-chain metrics show a massive 362,000 BTC demand gap opening up across major markets.

Bitcoin crashed below the key $70,000 support level on Friday, hitting a three-month low of $67,650 as a sudden leadership crisis at Nvidia, new MSCI index rules, and hot U.S. inflation rattled global markets.

Bitcoin fell 8.6% in 24 hours to $67,650 on early Friday, its lowest mark since August 19, extending a 10.2% weekly decline.

While yesterday’s pullback below $73,000 was driven largely by macroeconomic jitters, Friday’s breakdown reflects a rare convergence of tech-sector turmoil, institutional index risks, and evaporating spot liquidity.

Adding structural pressure to crypto equities, index provider MSCI’s November Index Review has placed Bitcoin treasury companies, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy (MSTR) and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, at risk of losing their place in major stock market indexes.

Under MSCI’s updated eligibility rules companies that hold too much of their assets in investments rather than running an operating business could lose their eligibility for indexes such as the MSCI USA and MSCI World.

When a company is dropped from a major index, funds that track it often have to sell their shares, which can drive down demand and put pressure on the stock price.

Strategy’s shares dropped 6.49% in extended trading on Thursday. The company has previously warned that eventual removal from MSCI indexes could force passive funds to sell around $2.8 billion worth of its shares.

For Bitcoin, the bigger concern is that Strategy could slow its Bitcoin purchases if it becomes harder or more expensive to raise money. That would remove a major source of buying demand just as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded five consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.43 billion, according to SoSoValue.

Market sentiment weakened further on November 12 after Nvidia announced that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was stepping down with immediate effect. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

Huang’s abrupt departure follows an internal board investigation and media reports detailing alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a alleged Chinese spy as well as relationships with Nvidia employees.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 4% on Thursday, extending a month-long decline that has wiped out 27.28% of the stock’s value. The Nvidia news added to pressure on risk assets, alongside declines in the Nasdaq Composite (-0.39%) and S&P 500 (-0.35%).

Rising inflation is adding pressure to both stock and crypto markets. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in higher than expected at 0.3%, against a forecast of 0.2%.

The higher-than-expected figures have reduced hopes of near-term interest rate cuts and raised expectations of a rate hike.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, markets are now pricing in an 88.5% chance of a 0.25-percentage-point rate increase in December. Higher interest rates could put further pressure on Bitcoin by making safer investments, such as U.S. Treasury bonds, more attractive

Blockchain data suggests Bitcoin lacked enough buying demand to defend the $70,000 level.

According to a CryptoQuant report, demand across spot and perpetual futures markets fell by 362,000 BTC over 30 days, with spot demand declining by 280,000 BTC and futures demand by 82,000 BTC.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin miner transfers to exchanges surged to 2,077 BTC on November 10, roughly 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. About 97% of the transfers came from Antpool.

At the same time, stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, pointing to declining liquidity across the crypto market.

According to CryptoQuant analysts, the broader picture remains cautious. Leverage is being unwound, but fresh spot buying has yet to return convincingly. Until demand strengthens, ETF flows turn positive and market liquidity stabilizes, Bitcoin’s recovery is likely to remain fragile, with further downside risks still in play.

#5154. Chainstack Traces Customer Data Breach to Exposed Admin Tools

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainstack’s expanded incident report focuses on access-control failures. Its recovery guidance makes completed credential rotation a priority.

Chainstack has added technical detail to the security incident it first disclosed on November 3. Its updated report, with a technical section dated November 10, describes an October intrusion built around configuration and access-control failures. The company says it found no evidence that a software vulnerability was exploited.

According to Chainstack, the attacker entered through a development Grafana instance with unchanged default administrator credentials. An unauthenticated tool server with broad Kubernetes permissions then formed part of the access path. Machine credentials also connected the development and production environments.

The operational lesson is about the reach of an account after the first login. A low-profile testing service can become consequential if it can contact sensitive systems or holds privileges that extend beyond its immediate job.

NewsBTC's coverage of the NEAR AI infrastructure incident explored a related boundary between an application and the services supporting it. The mechanisms differ, but both make the surrounding infrastructure relevant to a crypto platform's security.

The report identifies account names, organisation details, email addresses and password hashes as potentially exposed. It treats node credentials as exposed despite finding no evidence they were read, and asks customers to change passwords, rotate node credentials and regenerate platform API keys where used.

A password hash and a working access token create different problems. Hashes are representations of passwords, while an active token may directly authorise requests. Replacing a login password therefore cannot be assumed to invalidate every other credential associated with an application.

This is why incident guidance needs to identify the affected credential types clearly. A single instruction to change a password can leave developers uncertain about application endpoints, automated jobs and service integrations.

Chainstack's node-management documentation describes a staged rotation process. New credentials are generated while the existing ones remain active. Applications can then move to the replacements before the old credentials are deactivated.

The documentation says both sets continue working until that final step, with no automatic time limit. Completing the rotation permanently rejects requests using the previous credentials. It also says a node rotation does not change a multichain authentication token.

For an operator, the overlap reduces the risk of interrupting a working service while updating applications. The corresponding responsibility is to finish the migration. Generating a replacement alone leaves the previous means of access available.

A useful completion record would therefore track which applications have moved and when the old credentials were disabled. That is a practical control a team can verify after the initial emergency.

Grafana's security guidance warns that services on its local network may be reachable through its data-source proxy. It describes controls such as limiting permitted destinations and using firewall rules to restrict access to sensitive internal services.

Those precautions address what a tool can reach, as well as who can log into it. Authentication and network boundaries perform different jobs; permission limits provide another layer if either boundary fails.

NewsBTC's report on Chainalysis restoring screening services shows why operational recovery and data-exposure analysis can follow different timelines.

Chainstack's expanded account gives customers more detail to assess. The remaining test is whether access changes are completed and whether the revised controls can prevent one compromised service from reaching far beyond its intended role.

#5152. Bitcoin Faces First Back-to-Back Annual Losses in History, But There's a Catch

Bitcoin Faces First Back-to-Back Annual Losses in History, But There's a Catch

Bitcoin is flirting with a historical first that bulls probably don’t want to hear: Two consecutive years of losses, something the cryptocurrency has never experienced in its 18-year history.

The world's largest cryptocurrency finished 2025 down 6.34% and has lost another 15.65% so far in 2026, trading around $73,850 on November 10. If Bitcoin fails to recover above its annual opening price of roughly $87,500 before December 31, it will close two calendar years in the red for the first time.

Historical annual returns show Bitcoin has experienced several brutal crashes since its creation, but each negative calendar year has been followed by a positive one. Even the disastrous 2018 and 2022 bear markets failed to produce consecutive annual losses.

The historical pattern is clear. Its significance, however, deserves a closer look.

Bitcoin's previous annual crashes were considerably more painful than its current losing streak. The cryptocurrency plunged 73.56% in 2018 and another 64.27% in 2022, wiping out most of investors' holdings in each respective year.

By comparison, Bitcoin's 6.34% decline in 2025 was relatively mild. Add the roughly 16% loss recorded this year, and the combined decline comes to approximately 21% after accounting for compounding.

That's a fraction of the losses investors endured in previous crypto winters, despite the market potentially recording a longer sequence of negative annual returns.

Bitcoin's performance in 2024 also provides some perspective. The cryptocurrency surged more than 120% that year, meaning investors who bought at the beginning of 2024 would still be sitting on substantial gains despite the subsequent decline.

The picture changes considerably when measuring losses from the market's actual peak instead of calendar-year boundaries.

Bitcoin reached approximately $126,000 in October 2025 before crashing below $58,000 during 2026. That represented a decline exceeding 50%, a significantly more painful move than the 21% combined loss reflected in the two annual candlesticks.

Analysts have pointed to Bitcoin's increasingly institutional investor base, spot exchange-traded funds, and deeper market liquidity as potential explanations for its comparatively smaller bear-market drawdowns.

Those structural changes may help explain why Bitcoin's current market cycle looks different from previous ones, although they have not eliminated major price crashes.

There is also a distinction between the length of a losing streak and the severity of the losses. A market can decline slowly over several calendar years without inflicting the same damage as a single catastrophic year.

And Bitcoin has already demonstrated that a bad year doesn't necessarily translate into a prolonged downturn. The cryptocurrency gained roughly 92% in 2019 following its 2018 collapse and surged more than 155% in 2023 after its disastrous 2022 performance.

For now, Bitcoin has 50 days left in 2026 to avoid its first back-to-back annual losses. A third consecutive decline in 2027 would extend the streak further, but that scenario is still hypothetical.

At its November 10 price of approximately $73,850, Bitcoin would need to gain about 18.5% to recover its 2026 opening price and finish the year in positive territory.

#5150. NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

Home » Exchanges » NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

NYSE has selected Avalanche technology to support settlement for its planned tokenized securities platform, bringing round-the-clock stock trading and faster settlement closer to reality, pending regulatory approval.

The New York Stock Exchange is mixing together blockchain technology and traditional finance. It selected Avalanche to power the settlement infrastructure of its upcoming tokenized securities platform. The decision is part of a growing effort to bring crypto trading and its benefits to traditional finance.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the partnership will see Avalanche provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue. One of the goals is to enable round-the-clock trading, as well as clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, all of which still require regulatory changes.

NYSE has organized a yearlong test, and afterwards Avalanche emerged as a favorite provider and one that could meet its needs and provide a seamless inclusion of blockchain traders into the fold of the stock exchange account holders.

The platform is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks, meaning Avalanche will not necessarily host every tokenized stock traded through the venue. The technology will therefore mostly be used to record and settle transactions.

NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said that the focus was on speed, reliability, and predictable costs. Ava Labs CEO Emin Gün Sirer also highlighted the importance of dedicated infrastructure.

The crypto infrastructure industry is huge, and there’s a growing list of cryptocurrency exchanges, including those reviewed by CryptoManiaks, to choose from. Platforms made for transfers and smart contracts automating payments have also grown and now include thousands of providers. NYSE chose Avalanche due to some of its unique characteristics.

Avalanche’s architecture allows businesses to create dedicated blockchain networks with rules tailored to their operational and regulatory requirements. It creates a flexibility that traditional financial institutions are looking for.

Stock exchanges handle countless transactions, and stability is the most important feature they are looking for. Another important feature is atomic settlement. It allows the transfer of securities and corresponding payment to occur as part of the same transaction. Therefore, there’s no chance one side of a trade is completed while the other remains outstanding.

NYSE also plans to operate a custom blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than relying directly on Avalanche’s public network.

The decision reflects a broader effort to tokenize traditional markets and get the best of both worlds. That way, crypto companies won’t dominate the space, but can combine their features with those of the stock market.

Nasdaq is among the NYSE’s most prominent competitors. It, too, has developed tokenized stock infrastructure and is pursuing partnerships that could help distribute blockchain-based securities. This is done in cooperation with Kraken and in a way that NYSE is responding to the demands of a competitive market.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), a central institution in US securities settlements, also has plans to introduce tokenization. It plans to use blockchain to support securities custody and transfers.

NYSE has also expanded its list of partners. It now includes Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate. These developments show that financial institutions are fighting to establish the underlying infrastructure that will determine how digital securities are traded, transferred, and settled.

What Tokenized Stocks Could Mean for Investors

Tokenized stocks could change how investors are accessing traditional financial markets. The possibility of trading outside of business hours is the first thing investors have been looking for, alongside faster settlements. The NYSE’s broader platform plans include stablecoin-based funding, fractional share trading, and immediate settlement.

Ownership will also change. The NYSE has indicated that its platform will support tokenized shares that are fungible with traditionally issued securities, as well as securities originally issued in digital form. Shareholders will continue to have the same rights as traditional owners, meaning they’ll receive dividends and take part in corporate governance.

All of these benefits aren’t regulated, and before investors can take advantage of them, traditional regulatory bodies need to act and establish rules and guidelines for the new features.

Despite the institutional interest, the NYSE’s Avalanche-powered project still faces several challenges before it can become a functioning alternative to conventional securities infrastructure. The platform needs to demonstrate that it can maintain the safeguards expected of a major US stock exchange.

There’s also a distinction between Avalanche’s institutional adoption and the potential benefits for its native AVAX token. It’s not clear if the cooperation with NYSE will generate demand for AVAX. The project will depend on its ability to attract issuers, brokers, and investors while delivering reliable settlement.

#5149. Solo Brings Human Verification to Venmo Co-Founder’s JellyJelly App as AI Agents Beat CAPTCHA

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

“CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn’t. That’s becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people,” said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. “Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they’re dealing with a real person. Users shouldn’t have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it.”

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo’s SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone’s biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo’s human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

“Venmo made it easy to pay a friend,” said Magdon-Ismail. “The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I’m working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved.”

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

#5148. Dogecoin ETFs Mark One Month of Zero Activity

As Dogecoin continues to struggle amid prolonged crypto market volatility, its ETF performance has remained muted for the past week, drawing attention from market participants.

Although Dogecoin has retained its position as the king of all meme tokens, institutional demand for the leading meme token has remained on hold as it continues to post deeper price corrections.

Latest data from SosoValue shows that the U.S. Dogecoin spot ETFs have gone an entire month without recording any new inflows or outflows.

More specifically, the two existing spot DOGE ETFs last recorded activity on October 13, when they experienced a combined net outflow of $138,570.

The ETFs became muted the following day, October 14, and neither of the funds has registered a single day of positive or negative flows since then, leaving daily net inflows at zero until November 13.

As such, the Dogecoin ETFs have posted zero flows all month, signaling fading institutional interest in the world’s largest meme token by market capitalization despite its leading position in the memecoin market.

While institutional interest in Dogecoin appears to have declined significantly, both Dogecoin ETF issuers, Grayscale and 21Shares, recorded zero daily net inflows on November 13, confirming that the prolonged period of inactivity remains unchanged.

However, Grayscale's Dogecoin ETF has retained its dominance in the U.S. spot Dogecoin ETF market, holding a total of $9.15 million in net assets, while 21Shares' Dogecoin ETF has held only $1.58 million since its launch.

As such, Grayscale accounts for about 85.3% of the combined $10.73 million in assets held across the Dogecoin ETF market.

#5147. Deutsche Bank Goes Live With Crypto Custody After a Five-Year Buildup

Deutsche Bank Goes Live With Crypto Custody After a Five-Year Buildup

Five years after it first floated the idea, Germany’s largest lender is now holding Bitcoin for clients.

Deutsche Bank said Wednesday that its Digital Asset Custody service has gone live for paying clients, giving institutional and corporate customers in Europe a regulated way to store and transfer Bitcoin, Ethereum and three stablecoins: Circle’s USDC and EURC, plus EURAU.

The bank manages wallets and private keys on clients’ behalf. For now, the service covers custody and transfers, with tokenized financial instruments on its roadmap.

The service is aimed at clients of Deutsche Bank’s corporate and investment banking units, including corporations, asset managers, hedge funds, custodians, brokers and sovereign institutions, according to the bank’s September announcement of the plan.

Its setup includes hardware-based key protection, multi-person approvals and separate warm and cold storage, the bank said.

“In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, Deutsche Bank’s global head of trust and securities services.

Deutsche Bank also signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the majority-owned money manager formerly known as DWS, to explore working together on tokenized money market funds, crypto exchange-traded commodities and stablecoins.

The asset manager oversaw about 1.22 trillion euros as of Sept. 30. The bank has also said it plans to expand the custody service to Asia.

The launch caps a long road, going back to at least 2021 when Deutsche Bank began readying a crypto custody and trading platform. Then, in 2023, the bank applied for a digital asset custody license in Germany. Last year, reports said the bank planned to build the service with technology from crypto exchange Bitpanda, alongside its longtime partner Taurus.

Deutsche Bank received authorization from German regulator BaFin under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or MiCA, which requires crypto service providers to be licensed. The bank cautioned that its custody service doesn’t protect clients against swings in the value of digital assets, fraud or failures by other market participants.

The custody launch isn’t Deutsche Bank’s only crypto bet. The bank is among a group of global lenders, including Goldman Sachs and Citi, backing a $270 million challenge to crypto’s dominant stablecoin issuers.

#5146. Thailand SEC proposes 5 million Baht daily cap on stablecoin transfers — Why?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed a set of new rules to regulate stablecoin transactions conducted through licensed digital asset operators.

Announced on 12th November, the draft notification aims to prevent cryptocurrencies and stablecoins from being used for money laundering, cybercrime, and bypassing regulations governing international money transfers.

Here, it’s worth noting that this update came soon after September’s public consultation. During the same, the regulator collected feedback from industry participants.

As it stands, the SEC has incorporated those changes into the latest draft. It is now seeking further public comments until 26th November.

In this, one of the key proposals is to introduce a daily transfer limit of 5 million Thai baht per customer at each regulated digital asset operator. That said, the limit would apply separately to incoming and outgoing stablecoin transfers. However, the value of these transactions must also be consistent with the customer’s declared income and financial position.

However, it’s important to note that transfers between a customer’s own accounts at two SEC-supervised operators would be exempt from the limit, provided both operators follow the Travel Rule.

Simultaneously, the SEC also wants to strengthen wallet ownership verification. In this, the SEC has enabled customers to deposit stablecoins from their own verified wallets and withdraw them to wallets registered in their names.

Additionally, operators would also need to follow the Travel Rule, analyze customers, identify suspicious accounts, and track transactions connected to high-risk wallets.

These requirements would be done in order to make it harder for criminals to move illicit funds through regulated platforms.

Finally, the proposal also introduces stricter responsibilities for exchanges and brokers. Exchanges would have to publicly disclose their market makers and the digital assets for which they provide liquidity. Meanwhile, brokers would be prohibited from using liquidity providers for stablecoin-to-Thai baht trading pairs.

Besides that, brokers and dealers offering off-platform transactions would face a minimum transaction threshold of 3 million baht and would have to publish trading prices for transparency. Brokers would no longer be allowed to arrange off-platform trades directly between customers.

Taken together, these steps would help the SEC combat crimes that are concerning the stablecoin ecosystem in Thailand.
